drivingQuestion: Whose view does the mishna's 'ḥullin' clause follow, given it seems either impossible (R' Meir) or redundant (R' Yehuda)?
outcomeNote: The mishna is R' Yehuda with ḥullin taught tangentially; Ravina's alternative is refuted; the source is Num 30:3.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ טַעְמָא דְּאָמַר ״חוּלִּין שֶׁאוֹכַל לָךְ״ הָא אָמַר ״לַחוּלִּין שֶׁאוֹכַל לָךְ״, מַשְׁמַע: לָא לְחוּלִּין לֶיהֱוֵי אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» It may be inferred from the first case in the mishna that «the reason» the vow does not take effect is «that he said: That which I will eat of yours» will be «ḥullin; but» if «he said: That which I will eat of yours» will be «laḥullin,» that «indicates» that he is saying: It «will not [la] be non-sacred [ḥullin],» but «rather» like «an offering,» which is a vow that takes effect.

segments.he: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר — הָא לֵית לֵיהּ מִכְּלָל
segments.en: «Whose» opinion is expressed in «the mishna? If» it is the opinion of «Rabbi Meir, isn’t he of» the opinion that one does «not» say: «From»

segments.he: לָאו אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ הֵן! וְאֶלָּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַיְינוּ רֵישָׁא!
segments.en: «a negative» statement «you» can «infer a positive» statement? How then can it be inferred that it should be like an offering? «And» if it is «rather» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda,» who disagrees with Rabbi Meir in this matter, the ruling of the mishna is superfluous, as «this is» identical to the ruling of the mishna in «the first clause.» The mishna above (10b) already established that a vow that uses the term laḥullin takes effect.

segments.he: אַיְּידֵי דְּקָתָנֵי ״כִּבְשַׂר חֲזִיר״, ״כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה״, לְהָכִי קָתָנֵי ״חוּלִּין״.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: The ruling is superfluous. However, «since» the mishna «teaches» that the vow does not take effect when he says that the food will be «like pig meat» or «like» an object of «idol worship, it therefore teaches» incidentally that this ruling also applies when he says that it will be «non-sacred.»

segments.he: רָבִינָא אָמַר: הָכִי קָתָנֵי, וְאֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין: ״כְּחוּלִּין״, ״כִּבְשַׂר חֲזִיר״, ״כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה״. וְאִי לָא תְּנָא חוּלִּין, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא בָּעֵי שְׁאֵלָה.
segments.en: «Ravina said» that «this is» what the mishna «is teaching: And these are» the vows that do not take effect at all and therefore the item mentioned in the vow remains «permitted:» One who said that a certain item will be «like non-sacred» food, or «like pig meat,» or «like» an object of «idol worship. And if it did not teach» the case of «non-sacred» food, «I would say» that although the vow does not take effect, it still «requires,» by rabbinic law, «a request» to a halakhic authority for its dissolution.

segments.he: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְאַסּוֹקֵי עַל דַּעְתָּא הָכִי? הָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשְׁתּוֹ ״הֲרֵי אַתְּ עָלַי כְּאִימָּא״ — פּוֹתְחִין לוֹ פֶּתַח מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא לָא בָּעֲיָא שְׁאֵלָה! אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא, חוּלִּין מִמֵּילָא נַסְבַהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But is there» any reason «to consider this» interpretation? «But from» the fact «that the latter clause teaches» with regard to a man «who says to his wife: You are hereby to me like» my «mother,» that dissolution is «broached with him by» suggesting «a different extenuation, it may be inferred that» the vow in «the first clause does not necessitate a request» to a halakhic authority. «Rather,» the interpretation of Ravina must be rejected, and «it is clear» that the case of «non-sacred» food «was cited tangentially» to the other cases in the mishna.

segments.he: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר קְרָא: ״אִישׁ כִּי יִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַה׳״ — עַד שֶׁיִּדּוֹר בְּדָבָר הַנָּדוּר.
segments.en: § With regard to the principle that a prohibition cannot be created by associating a permitted item with one forbidden by Torah law, the Gemara asks: «From where is this matter» derived? The Gemara answers that «the verse states: “When a man takes a vow to the Lord”» (Numbers 30:3), which indicates that a vow does not take effect «until one takes a vow» by associating the status «of an item that is» forbidden by means of «a vow» with another item. If the item one is using to create the prohibition is forbidden by Torah law, the vow does not take effect.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ בְּדָבָר הָאָסוּר נָמֵי, דְּהָא כְּתִיב ״לֶאְסֹר אִסָּר עַל נַפְשׁוֹ״! ״לֶאְסֹר אִסָּר״ מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא: אֵיזֶהוּ אִיסָּר הָאָמוּר בַּתּוֹרָה כּוּ׳.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «If so,» then «even» if the item in the vow is associated «with an item forbidden» by Torah law, the vow should «also» take effect, «as» following that phrase in the verse «it is written: “To bind his soul with a bond [issar],”» which indicates that the association can be with an item forbidden [asur] by Torah law. The Gemara answers: The phrase «“To bind his soul with a bond” is necessary for that which is taught» in a baraita (12a): «What is the bond mentioned in the Torah.» The baraita derives from this phrase that a vow that associates the relevant item with an item whose prohibition was created by a pre-existing vow takes effect, but one whose prohibition is by Torah law does not take effect.
